bet.text: Shorten the cycle: take cones and cubes from the floor in any orientation, and shoot cubes over the charge station into the low nodes.

demand.text: A year later a team coach wrote that the team looked for an edge in a normal pick-and-place game, and that many design choices were shaped by expecting to fill a community cleanup role. By the championship it leaned toward cube shooting for playoffs.

cycle.text: A cube cycle covers about half the field, because cubes are shot over the charge station. Cones go from the floor to the arm. The operator picks the height; the driver stops roughly in front of a node and presses one button, and the robot drives to it and scores.

gave_up.text: The team tied its low chassis to a harder crossing of the charge station.

The coach later called the whole design overcomplicated and said that, apart from cube shooting, it did not make much sense: the arm pivoted at full height, and cones were not strictly controlled during part of the handoff. It worked fairly well eventually, but not as well as the team wanted.

changed.text: After a new rule change the team wanted more power to shoot over the charge station. It says braking the robot returns energy and raises battery voltage to about 15 V.
Off-season: it was picked for cube shooting at IRI and reached the finals, then built a replica of 2910's robot, which led to its 2024 design.

outcome.text: 49-15-1 in official play; ranked 17 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 71.09, Galileo).

facts.text: The bevel gear connects directly to the wheel as one custom machined part

functions.name: Intake as a ramp wheel

solves.text: Get a low robot over the charge station when its drive wheels lose contact

functions.type: intake acting as another wheel over the charge station

facts.text: It gets the robot over the ramp while the drive modules are off the ground

functions.name: Intake

solves.text: Take both pieces from the floor in any orientation and shorten the cycle

functions.type: floor roller intake that also shoots cubes

facts.text: An upper roller keeps cubes from being thrown away when the robot reaches them at speed
Side wheels index the cubes and also shoot them
Cubes are shot to place them on nodes and over the charge station into the low nodes
Welded flat belts about 1.2 to 1.5 mm thick carry the piece on the robot's floor, driven by the front roller; polycord was tried first and its welds were not flat and uniform enough

functions.name: Handoff to the arm
functions.type: transfer from floor intake to arm

facts.text: Cones go from the floor intake to the arm

cost.text: The coach says cones were not strictly controlled for part of the action

functions.name: Arm with differential wrist

solves.text: Turn the end effector two ways without motors up high

functions.type: arm with a two-motor differential wrist

facts.text: Moves the end effector in roll and in pitch with two motors at the base of the robot
Belts carry the motion up and need tensioners in several places

cost.text: The coach called having the arm pivot at full height part of an overcomplicated design

functions.name: Claw

solves.text: Open and close the claw while keeping the center of gravity low

functions.type: claw driven by cable from the base

facts.text: A motor at the bottom of the robot works the claw through a lead screw and a bicycle brake cable

cost.text: The cable cannot be twisted much, so the arm goes back to center during some movements to keep from tangling or damaging it

solves.text: Place cones on either side of the robot

facts.text: A servo turns the camera against a hard stop, so it stops at the same angle even though the servo is not very accurate

solves.text: Turn a cone picked up in any orientation the way the team wants it

facts.text: Detects the orientation of the cone; the arm then picks it up and reorients it without a button press
At the reveal it used classic image processing, not a trained network

solves.text: Line the robot up with a piece on the floor

facts.text: The driver heads in the general direction of a piece and the robot aligns to it
At the reveal it used a YOLO network, which the team called overkill: it believed classic methods would work unless a cube is in front of a blue bumper

At the reveal the team used only an assist mode, where the driver drives and software makes it more accurate, for pickup and placement; an automatic mode existed but it saw little value in it for this game
Runs on the same Raspberry Pi as the orientation camera, and is used along with the rotating Limelight

solves.text: Find the best arm route between any two states

facts.text: Arm states are a directed graph; a breadth-first search finds the route from the current position to the target
The operator chooses the placing height and blinks purple or yellow lights to ask the human player for a piece
The operator can change shooting angle and speed, reset sensors and correct game pieces during a match

decisions.choice: Shoot cubes over the charge station into low nodes
decisions.because: a cube cycle becomes about half a field long
decisions.instead_of: going to the double substation and then all the way to the nodes

decisions.choice: Put the motors at the bottom and carry motion up with belts
decisions.because: it keeps the center of gravity low, and belts are light and flexible in routing

decisions.choice: Turn the camera with a servo against hard stops
decisions.because: the servo does not have to be accurate

decisions.choice: Use braking energy for extra power on the shot over the charge station
decisions.because: the team says the returned energy raises battery voltage and gives extra shot power

decisions.choice: Design around a community cleanup role
decisions.because: the team was looking for an edge and expected certain teams to specialize in it
decisions.cost: the coach says the team was not willing to face that it was a normal pick-and-place game, and calls the design overcomplicated
